passage: I'm Chetan, and I've been where you are, Leela. You're worried your manager replied with just a thumbs-up to your long report? At twenty-four I sent a proposal to a client in the Gulf, and the client replied with a single thumbs-up. I took it as "approved" and started the work. Two days later he called, puzzled: he had only meant "received." In my office thumbs-up meant yes; in his it was a polite acknowledgment. Around then my niece in college sent folded hands to mean "please," my boss took it as thanks, and a colleague thought it meant praying. Nowadays, if it matters, I follow up in words: "Just to check, does thumbs-up mean go ahead?" It costs ten seconds.

qa.q: What had the client only meant by the thumbs-up?
How did Chetan probably feel when the client called two days later, puzzled?
qa.a: Chetan was probably surprised and embarrassed, having taken the thumbs-up as approval and already started the work.

qa.q: What could Leela do about the manager's thumbs-up?
qa.a: Leela can ask in words whether it means approved or just received.

qa.q: How did the client see his own thumbs-up?
qa.a: As a polite acknowledgment and not approval, which is why he was puzzled when Chetan started work.

grounding: Emoji such as a thumbs-up or folded hands mean different things across offices, ages and cultures, so a young adult checks intent.

passage: At the airport gate, with the boarding call blaring, Rafiq typed a fast reply to his manager Vinita's message about the client deck: "👍". Vinita, on a call in her own noisy corridor, read it as "sounds fine, go ahead." Rafiq had meant "seen, will check when I land." An hour later the deck went to the client without his edits. On landing he saw her message: "Thanks for approving 🙏." His stomach dropped. He rang her: "When I sent the thumbs-up, I meant I'd read it, not that it was approved. Sorry for not using words." Vinita paused, then laughed tiredly. "I should have asked. From now on, one line of text with the emoji?" They agreed.

qa.q: What did Rafiq type in reply to Vinita?
What was Rafiq thinking when he sent the thumbs-up?
qa.a: He meant he had seen it and would check when he landed, while Vinita took it as approval.

qa.q: What could Rafiq and Vinita do next time?
qa.a: They can add one line of text with the emoji, as they agreed.

qa.q: How might Vinita have felt when Rafiq called?
qa.a: Probably tired and a bit surprised, but she laughed, accepting a share of the responsibility.

grounding: A thumbs-up can mean received or approved, and under time pressure the mismatch is fixed by checking intent in words.
